subject: Chemistry

nodes.text: an atom is the smallest particle of an element that keeps the properties of that element
atoms are made of protons and neutrons in a central nucleus with electrons moving around it
protons carry positive charge, electrons carry negative charge, and neutrons are neutral
a molecule forms when two or more atoms join together by chemical bonds
a molecule of a compound contains atoms of different elements, like water having hydrogen and oxygen
a neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons so the charges balance

textbookPhrasings: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction.
A molecule is the smallest particle of an element or a compound that is capable of independent existence and shows all the properties of that substance.
Atoms consist of a nucleus containing protons and neutrons, surrounded by electrons revolving in orbits.
referenceFacts: An atom is the smallest particle of an element
The nucleus contains protons and neutrons
Protons have a positive charge and electrons have a negative charge
A molecule is formed when two or more atoms bond together
A compound contains atoms of different elements
A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons

whyQuestions.q: Why is a whole atom electrically neutral even though it contains charged particles?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: it has equal numbers of positive protons and negative electrons, so the charges cancel

whyQuestions.q: Why is water called a compound but oxygen gas is called an element?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: water's molecule contains atoms of two different elements, while oxygen gas has atoms of only one element

whyQuestions.q: Why do atoms bond together to form molecules instead of staying separate?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: bonding lets atoms reach a more stable, lower-energy arrangement

misconceptions: Atoms are the same thing as molecules
Electrons sit still inside the nucleus
An atom has more protons than electrons and is therefore charged
